source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: O Rama, formerly in the Treta Yuga, there was a very extensive area, a hundred yojanas all around, that was devoid of both animals and birds.
verses.2: O gentle one, I approached that uninhabited forest to perform excellent penance and to traverse it.
verses.3: The beauty of that forest, with its various kinds of trees bearing fruits and roots of pleasant taste, was indeed indescribable.
verses.4: In the middle of that forest was a lake, a yojana in length, teeming with swans and karandava ducks, and graced by chakravaka birds.
verses.5: That lake was filled with lotuses and water lilies, free from moss, exceedingly wonderful, and its water was of unsurpassed pleasant taste.
verses.6: The lake was pure, undisturbed, glorious, and filled with flocks of birds; and near it was a great and wonderful hermitage.
verses.7: O best among men, that hermitage was ancient, exceedingly sacred, yet devoid of ascetics, and there I spent a summer night.
verses.8: Early in the morning, having risen, I approached that lake, and there I saw a very well-nourished, undecaying corpse somewhere.
verses.9: O King, it was resting in that body of water, its limbs nourished by the rich environment, remaining there with supreme splendor.
verses.10: O Raghava, O Lord, pondering that matter, I remained on the lake shore for a moment, wondering what this might be.
verses.11: Then, after a moment, I saw a divine aerial chariot of wondrous sight, exceedingly grand, yoked with swans, and swift as thought.
verses.12: O Raghunandana, O hero, a thousand Apsaras adorned with divine ornaments served that exceedingly celestial being in the aerial chariot.
verses.13: Some (celestial women) sing divine songs, others play musical instruments, some engage in playful sports, and still others dance.
verses.14: Other celestial women fanned his lotus-eyed face with whisks that had golden handles and shone like moonbeams.
verses.15: Then, O Rama, O delight of the Raghus, while I watched, that celestial being, like the sun leaving the peak of Meru, descended from his celestial chariot, abandoned his throne, and proceeded to eat that corpse.
verses.16: After thus eating a large quantity of very plump meat to his heart's content, the celestial being descended into a lake and began to perform ablutions.
verses.17: Having performed ablutions properly, O foremost of the Raghus, that celestial being then began to ascend his excellent and best celestial chariot.
verses.18: Having seen that god-like being ascending, I then spoke these words to the celestial being, O best among men.
verses.19: O god-like one, who are you, and why do you consume this reprehensible food, O gentle one, please tell me the reason.
verses.20: Whose nature would be such, and what kind of food is this that is approved by gods; O gentle one, this is a wonder, and I truly wish to hear about it.
verses.21: I do not consider this corpse to be suitable food for you.
verses.22: O king, thus addressed, that celestial being, out of curiosity and with pleasant and truthful words, having heard all my words, then narrated everything to me. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 77 ।। Thus ends the seventy-seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
